f: A portrait of Kaldor, painted by somebody who very much wanted to keep their hands. Each is more flattering than the last.
The fortieth isn't Kaldor at all. It's just the sun.
Z: A small statue of Kaldor, holding a smaller statue of Kaldor.
W: Gold leaf on the walls, peeling. Under it, the old Hale stone, plain and grey.
1: The way out, to the bazaar.

objects.name: Sim Fawnley
lines: Welcome to the Hall of Kaldor! Forty portraits! One king! Please don't say anything about the nose.
I'm the curator. I curate. Mostly I check nobody's said anything about the nose.

answer: NOTHING. There is nothing about the nose. The nose is perfect.
…The first painter painted it as it is. Nobody's seen him since. Portrait two onward: perfect nose.

questions.ask: Why is the last one the sun?
answer: The fortieth painter ran out of ways to flatter him. So he painted the sun and called it 'Kaldor, Roughly'.
The king loved it. It's his favourite. Don't tell him it's the sun.

lines: Underneath, small: Exit through the gift shop. (There is no gift shop. Kaldor took it.)
Behind the fortieth portrait, the one that's just the sun: a Heart Piece.
The painter hid it there. He wanted somebody to find something real in here.
